title: Preemptive cohorting and probe holdoff to reduce HPA/KEDA false scale events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident investigation and action plan after a series of small capacity blips where KEDA/HPA combinations produced noisy up/down scale events leading to transient cold starts for inference tenants. The focus of this ticket is to implement preemptive cohorting, probe holdoff windows, and signal attenuation to reduce false positives and negative scaling decisions while preserving latency SLOs.
incident_summary: Between 2026-02-26 and 2026-02-28 we observed three short-lived autoscaler oscillations in our EU cluster. Each oscillation coincided with noisy metrics from the request-rate KEDA scaler combined with probe jitter on the warm-pool controller, resulting in repeated node additions and removals and ~40s median cold-start regressions for affected model routes.
timeline: 2026-02-26 03:14 UTC: first scale-up spike detected; 03:17 UTC: rapid scale-down; 03:20 UTC: second scale-up; 03:25 UTC: mitigation rule applied (manual warm-pool lock); 2026-02-27: began metric filtering trial for request-rate scaler; 2026-02-28: reverted to conservative holdoff for critical routes.
root_cause: Primary cause was high-frequency noise in external ingress rate metrics combined with a short (30s) scaling holdoff which allowed KEDA to trigger multiple rapid scale-outs. Secondary cause: warm-pool probe eviction timing overlapped with scale actions, causing the warm pool to be perceived as cold and triggering additional provisioning.
mitigations_taken: Applied a temporary 120s scale-in cooldown on KEDA triggers for the EU cluster
Locked warm-pool size for customer-facing inference lanes while we diagnose
Throttled external synthetic traffic generator to rule out test traffic artefacts
action_items: ENG-489201-A1: Implement cohorting bucket for request-rate scaler (owner: Marc Chen, due: 2026-03-11)
ENG-489201-A2: Add probe holdoff heuristic to warm-pool controller (owner: Jana Müller, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-489201-A3: Introduce percentile-based smoothing (P95->P90 delta) on KEDA scaler input (owner: Ravi Singh, due: 2026-03-14)
ENG-489201-A4: Add runbook entry for manual warm-pool lock and quick rollback (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-10)
ENG-489201-A5: Create e2e test harness simulating noisy ingress to validate holdoff parameters (owner: QA Team, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-489201-A6: Add dashboard panels for probe evictions vs scale events (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-489201-A7: Feature-flag rollout plan for adaptive holdoff (owner: Marc Chen, due: 2026-03-21)
decision_notes: We decided to pursue a layered approach rather than a single global cooldown: 1) cohorting of similar traffic patterns to prevent noisy tenants from affecting others, 2) probe holdoff on the warm-pool controller to avoid eviction-triggered cold starts during close-proximity scale events, and 3) percentile smoothing on KEDA input metrics. This preserves fast scaling for genuine spikes while reducing oscillation risk.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy probe holdoff and smoothing to 10% of EU capacity with feature flag off by default. Phase 1: enable cohorting for low-risk internal tenants and monitor for 48h. Phase 2: expand to all tenants with gradual ramp over 72h. Emergency revert via warm-pool lock and disable smoothing flag.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for smoothing and holdoff logic. 2) Integration tests with KEDA simulated triggers. 3) e2e chaos test that injects 5-15% synthetic request-rate noise and validates no >2 scale cycles in 10 minutes. 4) Canary run against internal performance tenants before customer-facing rollout.
observability_changes: New Grafana panel: 'Scaler Input Noise' (rolling stddev of request-rate)
Alert: 'RepeatedScaleOscillation' if >2 scale events in 10m for same pool
Trace link between probe eviction events and scale actions in X-Ray traces
